h: From Jet Engines to Kart Engines
p: Farnborough's link with flight runs deep. This is where British powered flight got going in the early 1900s, and the Royal Aircraft Establishment worked here for decades. The Farnborough Air Sciences Trust Museum, known as FAST, tells that story with aircraft, models and exhibits, and it's run by enthusiasts who know their stuff. It makes a great add-on for anyone in your group who loves machines.

The famous Farnborough International Airshow is held every other year, in even-numbered years, in July. It's a trade show for much of the week with public days at the end, and the whole area gets very busy around then, so plan any visit carefully if your race coincides.

Back to the karting. Pilots will tell you that smooth inputs matter, and it's exactly the same in a kart. Gentle steering, progressive braking and a calm right foot will usually beat the white-knuckle approach.

If you're travelling in by train, Farnborough has two stations, Farnborough Main and Farnborough North, giving links towards London Waterloo and across to Reading and Guildford. It makes life easy if your group is coming from different directions and nobody wants to be the designated driver.

For a gentler wind-down, the Basingstoke Canal runs nearby and has towpaths for a peaceful walk,. Farnborough is well placed for the M3, so it's an easy reach from London and across Hampshire and Surrey.
